## Judged

- **judged-sealed-wall-refusal-vocabulary** [accepted-deviation]: AC-3's sealed-wall refusal reaches CLI users in board-surface vocabulary: the shared core hard-codes the action name "stub-instantiate" and speaks of a "wall" (SealedFeatureWallGuard in internal/stubinstantiate/stubinstantiate.go), so `verdi design start --from-stub` against a non-accepted feature prints e.g. "stub-instantiate is only available on an accepted-pending-build spec... this wall's status is draft" — the refusal names its reason (satisfying the letter of ac-3), but a CLI operator who never typed "stub-instantiate" and has no board "wall" in view gets another surface's terms. This is a deliberate consequence of byte-identical shared-core messages (the parity property ac-3 also demands), so it may be accepted intent rather than drift. (confidence 0.25) — Accepted as the deliberate consequence of the property ac-3 itself demands: the board action and the CLI call one shared core with proven byte-identical output (the parity assertion), so the refusal text is necessarily one vocabulary — and the chosen vocabulary is the board's because the wall is where the sealed-record register law lives. Rewording per surface would reintroduce exactly the two-surfaces-drift class the one-core design eliminated; the refusal still names its reason and the actual status, satisfying ac-3's substance. Reversible follow-up if the vocabulary ever matters more than parity: a surface parameter on the shared constructor, with the parity assertion widened to cover both renderings.
